8. Before we go into the scope and effect of Section 80 of
the CPC, we may look at the allegations and reliefs claimed in
D the suit. As noted herein earlier, the trial court decided the is-sue, namely, issue No.4 on the ground that the respondent No.3

respondent No.3 was not necessary, whereas the High Court

to dismiss the suit in its entirety. Let us now look into the allega-tions made in the plaint as well as the reliefs claimed in the
F same. The land of the appellants was acquired by respondent
Nos. 1 an<] 2 and in lieu thereof, possession, as described in

no order was passed by the District Education Officer, which
